You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC pattern notes

## Reflection tiling: 3×2 copies

Observed rule from task-83647a27 demos and the solved test: take the entire input grid and tile it into 3 rows × 2 columns of copies. Across the two horizontal tiles, use a left-right reflection in the left tile and the original orientation in the right tile. Across vertical tiles, use top-bottom reflection for the top and bottom tile rows, and the original orientation for the middle tile row. Apply both reflections in the top-left and bottom-left tiles as appropriate (reflections compose).

Thus output dimensions are 3H × 2W. For input coordinate (r,c), its output appears in each tile at the transformed coordinate given by that tile's optional vertical/horizontal reflection. Example: a single pixel at input (r=1,c=5) in a 5×7 grid appears at output 0-based positions (3,1), (6,5), (13,1), (3,12), (6,12), (13,12), matching the demo's output (1-based rows 4,7,14 and columns 2,7,14? Note: demo had source c=5 zero-based, so right copy is c=12 zero-based / column 13 one-based; middle tile left copy c=5 zero-based / column 6 one-based). Verify coordinates against the grid dimensions when reusing.

Evidence: task-83647a27 demo 1 (2×6→6×12), demo 2 (5×7→15×14), and its test (2×10→6×20) all match this tiling/reflection rule.

## Hollow rectangular frames: fill by interior side-length parity
Evidence: task-87f587a7 demonstrations and solved test.

When an outline encloses a rectangular empty interior, fill the interior uniformly based on its dimensions: an odd-by-odd interior is color 7; an even-by-even interior is color 2. Leave the outline and exterior unchanged. Examples: 1x1 interior -> 7; 2x2 -> 2; 3x3 -> 7; 4x4 -> 2; 5x5 -> 7; 6x6 -> 2. This applied regardless of the outline color (seen with colors 1, 3, 5, 6, 8).

Solved instance included frames with 1x1, 2x2, and 6x6 interiors, filled 7, 2, and 2 respectively. The original mistake was assigning color 2 to the 1x1 interior.
